Events.RelatedDescription: Opened issue ".NET 11 Release Candidate 1" (#444) at dotnet/announcements
Events.RelatedBody:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10569. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 1. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc1).

This is our first of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

# Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69304 – ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core IIS out-of-process hosting and request decompression. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The IIS Middleware for ASP.NET Core did not properly constrain decompression of certain types of request, leading to excess memory consumption and a Denial of Service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69155 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-409 (Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows / IIS out-of-process - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.1 Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.19 | 9.0.20 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.19 | 9.0.20 ### .NET 8 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69806 – .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet-watch AspireServerService exposes information through the use of certain arguments, that in turn can enable code injection. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56167 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.0 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor); CWE-94 (Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects Linux installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks) on Linux, you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart dotnet watch and your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-69806](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-69806) ### Acknowledgements Ky0toFu with Microsoft ### Revisions V1.0 (09/08/2026): Advisory published.

Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native can perform an out of bounds write while processing MSFZ PDB files. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/133438 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-122 (Heap-based Buffer Overflow) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.10.0-beta1.24272.1, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 10 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 9 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 8 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET or Visual Studio. 2. If your application references Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native, update the package reference to version 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 or later. Once you have installed the updated runtime, SDK, Visual Studio, or package, restart your apps for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-58649 – .NET Information Disclosure Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet watch BrowserRefreshServer does not adequately validate cross-origin WebSocket origins, potentially allowing IL and PDB information disclosure. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56166 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 6.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-346 (Origin Validation Error) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.1xx | >= 9.0.100, <= 9.0.119 | 9.0.120 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ### .NET 8 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 8.0.1xx | >= 8.0.100, <= 8.0.129 | 8.0.130 8.0.4xx | >= 8.0.400, <= 8.0.423 | 8.0.424 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart dotnet watch and your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem" (#1792)

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:
  - [Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects)
    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**
- This issue appears on windows server machines but the software runs on different machines and I would like to avoid temporary workarounds such as editing the registry and activate the strong name bypass feature because of the forced validation on windows server machines

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

We have directed your feedback to the appropriate engineering team for further evaluation. The team will review the feedback and notify you about the next steps.

Because we print a lot, we really suffer from this performance penalty.

Also reading PaperSizes and PaperSources from the printer settings is slow caused by the same problem.

Could you please inform me about a possible fix?

Best Regards,

Raphael

In my opinion the fix is easy: replace GetOutputPort by OutputPort in the call to

FastDeviceCapabilities.

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Optimize array Where spreads for mutable list interfaces
Issues.Body:
## Summary

This change still needs language-design approval to allow the relevant `System.Linq.Enumerable` calls in collection-expression lowering. [Specification review](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/85777#issuecomment-5817059528).

Optimize a narrowly matched collection-expression lowering:

```csharp
IList<T> result = [.. array.Where(predicate)];
ICollection<T> result = [.. array.Where(predicate)];
```

For a single spread over the non-indexed `System.Linq.Enumerable.Where<T>` whose source is a same-element-type SZArray, lower through the existing optional `Enumerable.ToList<T>` path. All other shapes retain the existing `List<T>`/`AddRange` fallback.

This is related to dotnet/runtime#114074, but does not claim to fix that issue in general and does not change Runtime `List<T>.AddRange`.

## Correctness scope

The optimization requires:

- a mutable `IList<T>` or `ICollection<T>` collection expression;
- exactly one spread and no explicit `with` collection creation;
- the exact optional well-known non-indexed `Enumerable.Where<T>` member;
- the normal two-argument mapping, excluding reordered arguments;
- a same-`T` SZArray source; and
- no non-identity per-element conversion.

Indexed or user-defined `Where` calls, saved/assigned iterators, list and arbitrary enumerable sources, mixed elements, read-only interfaces, explicit capacity, covariance requiring an element conversion, and other conversion cases keep the existing lowering. Missing `Where` or `ToList` well-known members also fall back.

The returned concrete `List<T>` may have a different observable `Capacity` after a cast. Capacity is not part of the collection-expression interface conversion contract; the measured cold capacities changed from 131,072 to 100,000 and from 1,048,576 to 1,000,000 for the two primary sizes.

## Validation

Reported build command:

```sh
.dotnet/dotnet build src/Compilers/CSharp/csc/AnyCpu/csc.csproj \
  -c Release -f net10.0 -m:1 -nr:false \
  -p:RunAnalyzersDuringBuild=true -p:BuildInParallel=false \
  -p:UseSharedCompilation=false -p:RestoreDisableParallel=true \
  -p:RestoreUseStaticGraphEvaluation=false
```

Baseline and candidate builds completed with zero warnings and errors.

Reported test command:

```sh
.dotnet/dotnet test src/Compilers/CSharp/Test/Emit3/Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Emit3.UnitTests.csproj \
  -c Release -f net10.0 --no-build --no-restore \
  --filter FullyQualifiedName~CollectionExpressionTests \
  --logger 'trx;LogFileName=collection-expressions-arm64.trx'
```

Result: 2,026 executed and passed, 0 failed; 8 of 2,034 discovered cases were reported skipped. The new IL, exception/evaluation-order, mutation, exclusion, and optional-member tests passed. `dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes` also passed for the four edited files.

## Performance

The current measurements use BenchmarkDotNet with `MemoryDiagnoser`. [All 36 cases, individual launch means, and reproduction source](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/85777#issuecomment-5817851995) are in the timing follow-up.

Both saved compilers compiled the same source against the same reference assemblies. BDN loads the resulting assemblies and measures one operation per invocation. Setup, reflection, and result checks run outside timing.

Environment: Apple M4 Pro, 12 cores, 48 GiB, macOS 26.5.1 arm64; pinned Runtime `935105343cbab1bafa63362e31d1e8638248b463` (.NET 12.0.0-dev). BDN `0.16.0-nightly.20260801.595`; driver SDK `11.0.100-rc.1.26420.103`; measured child processes use the pinned CoreRun.

Each case ran in a separate process in six passes ordered A/B/B/A/A/B. Each launch had five warmup iterations and ten measured iterations, with a requested iteration time of 200 ms. Values below average the three launch means per variant.

| Input (`IList<int>`, all match) | Base time | PR time | Time change | Base B/op | PR B/op |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100,000 elements | 281.18 us | 75.76 us | -73.1% | 1,050,300.3 | 400,674.3 |
| 1,000,000 elements | 2,782.88 us | 636.63 us | -77.1% | 8,389,263.3 | 4,001,258.3 |
| 8 elements | 29.88 ns | 21.80 ns | -27.0% | 176 | 136 |
| 1 element | 16.02 ns | 18.59 ns | +16.0% | 120 | 112 |

The one-element input is a CPU regression despite allocating fewer bytes. The two interface targets were about 2.6-2.7 ns slower per operation for this case. For 100,000-element arrays, no-match and first-16-match `IList<int>` cases took 66.96 to 22.68 us and 40.92 to 23.34 us, respectively. `ICollection<int>` showed the same pattern. The complete table retains all unchanged controls and slower results.

These are warm microbenchmarks on a shared Mac, with the same delegate overhead in both variants. Preliminary A/A launch means varied by 0.4-4.1% across four cases. Small changes in unchanged controls should not be interpreted as established gains or regressions. BDN's usual within-launch outlier handling applies; no case or launch was removed based on whether the PR was faster.

The original allocation-only investigation used `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread`. Its warm results have been superseded here by the BDN measurements. Its separate cold observations were one fresh process and one operation per case, without warmup: 1,049,080 to 926,016 B/op for 100,000 elements and 8,389,184 to 8,196,112 B/op for 1,000,000 elements, for both interface targets. Those single observations are not BDN results and do not establish cold CPU performance.

ArrayPool reuse contributes to the warm results. First-call time, other platforms, other Runtime versions, and alternative LINQ implementations have not been measured.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI systems assisted with the design, implementation, evidence preparation, and independent review of this change. Build, test, and measurement results above are reported from the experiment receipts and should receive normal human maintainer review.

Issues.Title: Compiler stack overflow on self-referential nullable union with updated-memory-safety-rules
Issues.Body:
Repro:
```csharp
public union NullableNat(bool, NullableNat?);
```
Compile as a library with `/langversion:preview /nullable:enable /features:updated-memory-safety-rules` and .NET 11 reference assemblies.

Compiler `5.12.0-1.26463.105` succeeds. Compiler `5.12.0-1.26471.108` stack-overflows; the latter succeeds without the feature flag.

The recursive stack goes through `SourceMemberContainerTypeSymbol.AddSynthesizedTypeMembersIfNecessary`, `Binder.BindType`, and `Binder.ReportDiagnosticsIfUnsafeMemberAccess` / `checkTypeArgumentWithConstructorConstraint`, which accesses `InstanceConstructors` while union members are being synthesized.

This blocks dotnet/runtime#134394. CI build: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1609539. The constraint-check changes in https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/84888 appear relevant. The same failure reproduces locally on macOS arm64 compiling System.Text.Json.Tests.

Expected: Successful compilation without disabling updated memory-safety checks.

> [!NOTE]
> This issue was generated by GitHub Copilot.

Issues.Title: Bound RunTests timeout dump collection
Issues.Body:
RunTests timeout handling could hang indefinitely while collecting dumps, preventing cancellation and cleanup of test processes. This was observed in Azure build [1608536](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1608536&view=logs&j=619f5e54-57a1-505e-89d3-7fd9a967ab59&t=2c62285d-5c4e-5696-2c9f-bff3060420b3), where timeout diagnostics started but never reached test-runner cleanup before the job-level timeout.

- **Bounded external dump collection**
  - Replaced unbounded in-process dump collection with pinned local `dotnet-dump`.
  - Runs:
    ```sh
    dotnet tool run dotnet-dump -- collect --process-id <pid> --type Full --output <path>
    ```
  - Adds a 2-minute per-process collector timeout.
  - On timeout, kills only the collector process tree and preserves any partial dump file.

- **Timeout cleanup ordering**
  - Moves test-runner cancellation into a `finally` path so cleanup runs regardless of dump success, failure, cancellation, or timeout.
  - Updates process cancellation to terminate child process trees.

- **Diagnostics and logging**
  - Logs target process ID/name, dump path, collector command, timeout, and result.
  - Flushes `runtests.log` before and after dump attempts so diagnostics survive a stuck collector.
  - Reports success only when the collector exits successfully and the expected dump exists.

- **Focused coverage**
  - Adds RunTests unit coverage for:
    - successful dump collection
    - nonzero collector exit
    - missing dump output
    - hung collector timeout/termination
    - test-runner cleanup after bounded diagnostics

Validation performed:
- `dotnet build src/Tools/RunTests/UnitTests/RunTests.UnitTests.csproj`
- `dotnet test src/Tools/RunTests/UnitTests/RunTests.UnitTests.csproj --no-build`
- `dotnet test src/Tools/RunTests/RunTests.sln --no-build`

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Fix Roslyn RunTests timeout dump collection so a hung dump operation cannot prevent test-process cleanup, and open a PR with the implementation.
> 
> Context and proven failure:
> - Azure build 1608536, job Test_Windows_CoreClr_Debug_Single_Machine, timed out in RunTests.
> - RunTests' 90-minute timeout fired and produced timeout.png, then produced no output until Azure canceled the 120-minute job.
> - src/Tools/RunTests/Program.cs awaits HandleTimeout before calling cts.Cancel(), so a blocked diagnostic operation prevents cancellation/killing of test runners.
> - src/Tools/RunTests/DumpCollector.cs currently calls DiagnosticsClient.WriteDump synchronously without a deadline or cancellation. The dump of the hung CoreCLR testhost did not return.
> - The pre-dump status uses ConsoleUtil.Write without a newline, and the log file is persisted only after the dump loop, leaving no useful diagnostics when collection hangs.
> - Relevant regression: https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/84227
> - Failing build: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1608536&view=logs&j=619f5e54-57a1-505e-89d3-7fd9a967ab59&t=2c62285d-5c4e-5696-2c9f-bff3060420b3
> 
> Implement a cross-platform, bounded dump-collection design:
> 1. Run dotnet-dump as an out-of-process collector rather than directly blocking in DiagnosticsClient.WriteDump. Use `dotnet-dump collect --process-id <pid> --type Full --output <path>` (or the repository-standard equivalent).
> 2. Pin/provision dotnet-dump reproducibly using existing Roslyn/Arcade dependency and tool-management conventions. Do not depend on an unversioned machine-global installation. Reuse existing infrastructure if dotnet-dump is already provisioned.
> 3. Give each dump attempt a short explicit timeout (choose and document a reasonable value). On expiry, terminate only the collector process tree and proceed.
> 4. Ensure test-runner cancellation/termination occurs in a finally path regardless of dump success, failure, cancellation, or timeout. Diagnostic collection must never consume the remaining Azure job indefinitely.
> 5. Log and flush the target process ID, process name, output path, collector command/path, completion/failure, and timeout before/when each operation occurs. Ensure runtests.log is written even when collection fails or hangs.
> 6. Preserve partial dump files when useful and do not report success unless the collector exits successfully and the expected output exists.
> 7. Keep behavior cross-platform. Note that dotnet-dump uses native MiniDumpWriteDump on Windows and runtime diagnostics IPC on Unix; the external deadline is still required on every platform.
> 8. Avoid unrelated changes.
> 
> Testing requirements:
> - Add focused tests around the timeout/dump orchestration, including a fake collector that never exits, proving the collector is terminated and test cleanup still runs.
> - Cover collector nonzero exit/missing output and successful collection as practical.
> - Run the smallest relevant build/test suite and include results in the PR description.
> - Review existing process helpers and cancellation patterns before adding new infrastructure.
> 
> The PR description should link the failing Azure build and explain the causal chain and why an external bounded collector fixes it. If repository constraints make dotnet-dump unsuitable, document the concrete blocker in the PR and implement the closest cross-platform bounded out-of-process alternative; do not fall back to another unbounded in-process call.


</details>

Issues.Title: Normalize interceptor argument ref kinds for reduced extension calls
Issues.Body:
Reduced interceptor extension calls could copy `RefKind.RefReadOnlyParameter` directly into `argumentRefKindsOpt`, although that value is only valid for parameters, not arguments.

- **Lowering**
  - Convert synthesized parameter ref kinds through the existing parameter-to-argument mapping.
  - Preserve correct `in`/strict-in semantics for `ref readonly` receivers.

```csharp
argumentRefKindsOpt =
    SyntheticBoundNodeFactory.ArgumentRefKindsFromParameterRefKinds(
        method, useStrictArgumentRefKinds: false);
```

- **Regression coverage**

Issues.Title: LocalRewriter.InterceptCallAndAdjustArguments possibly adds unsupported values to  `argumentRefKindsOpt` array
Issues.Body:
In general, parameter ref kind can be `RefKind.RefReadOnlyParameter`, which is not expected as an argument ref kind. For example, see code in `LocalRewriter.GetEffectiveRefKind`:
https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/a71a1ceec84809e463f6781f944819ed0fb48205/src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Lowering/LocalRewriter/LocalRewriter_Call.cs#L1282-L1294 

Or in `SyntheticBoundNodeFactory.ArgumentRefKindFromParameterRefKind`:
https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/a71a1ceec84809e463f6781f944819ed0fb48205/src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Lowering/SyntheticBoundNodeFactory.cs#L913-L921

There are two places in `LocalRewriter.InterceptCallAndAdjustArguments` that simply put parameter ref kind into argument ref kinds array:

https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/a71a1ceec84809e463f6781f944819ed0fb48205/src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Lowering/LocalRewriter/LocalRewriter_Call.cs#L322

https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/a71a1ceec84809e463f6781f944819ed0fb48205/src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Lowering/LocalRewriter/LocalRewriter_Call.cs#L327

It is quite possible, that for the first code path we expect all parameter ref kinds to be `RefKind.None`. Then, perhaps, we should assert the fact and use `RefKind.None` values explicitly. 
It doesn't look like we can make any assumptions about `thisRefKind` value used by the second code path.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "LocalRewriter.InterceptCallAndAdjustArguments possibly adds unsupported values to  `argumentRefKindsOpt` array" (#85759)

Issues.Title: [ResourceLock] Narrow GivenAPickBestRidMultiThreading serialization to the CWD-mutating test
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Replaces the class-level `[DoNotParallelize]` on `GivenAPickBestRidMultiThreading`
(`test/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests`, `MSTestParallelizeScope=ClassLevel`) with a
method-level `[ResourceLock(WellKnownResources.CurrentDirectory)]` on the one test that
actually mutates the process-wide current directory.

## Shared resource and conflicting tests

`ItResolvesRelativeRuntimeGraphPathAgainstProjectDirectory` calls
`Directory.SetCurrentDirectory(decoyCwd)` to prove `PickBestRid` resolves a relative
`RuntimeGraphPath` via `TaskEnvironment`, not `Environment.CurrentDirectory`/process CWD.
That mutation is process-wide and can race any other test in the assembly that reads or
sets the current directory (for example the CWD probes in
`GivenATaskEnvironmentDefault`, `GivenAGenerateClsidMapMultiThreading`, and similar
"decoy CWD" tests elsewhere in this project). `WellKnownResources.CurrentDirectory` is
the shared constant already used for this exact resource by
`GivenAGetDependsOnNETStandardMultiThreading` in the sibling
`Microsoft.NET.Build.Extensions.Tasks.Tests` project.

The other two tests in the class,
`MissingFileErrorContainsOriginalRelativePathNotAbsolutized` and
`EmptyRuntimeGraphPathLogsMissingFileError`, only create/read a project directory via
`TaskEnvironmentHelper.CreateForTest(projectDir)` and never touch the process CWD or any
other process-global state, so they no longer need to be deferred to the serial tail.

## Why this attribute placement is minimal

- The lock is method-level, not class-level, because only one of the three tests in the
  class touches the shared resource.
- `[ResourceLock]` (not `[DoNotParallelize]`) is used because a resource lock gives the
  same mutual exclusion for the CWD mutation without deferring the whole class to the
  end of the parallel run — the other two tests can now run in the normal parallel set.
- `WellKnownResources.CurrentDirectory` is used instead of a bare string literal, per
  MSTEST0073 (`PreferConstantForResourceLockAnalyzer`), which is a build error in this
  project (`MSTestAnalysisMode=Recommended` + `TreatWarningsAsErrors`).

This class was already parallelization-opted-in (`MSTestParallelizeScope=ClassLevel`),
so this is a live throughput/over-serialization fix, not a preparation-only change.

## Validation

Bootstrapped the repo-local SDK with `bash ./restore.sh` (`.dotnet/dotnet` was not
present), then ran the focused class through the `run-tests` skill's runner:

```
./.dotnet/dotnet scripts/RunTests.cs -- \
  --project test/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests.csproj \
  --filter "FullyQualifiedName~GivenAPickBestRidMultiThreading" --skip-redist-check
```

Result: **4 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (also confirms MSTEST0073-0077 raised no
errors for the new declaration). `--skip-redist-check` was used because this test-only
change to `Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests` does not consume `artifacts/bin/redist`.

Detection runs exposed preventable workflow failures when transient GitHub connectivity problems occurred: Issue Triage deliberately removed every compatible cached Copilot CLI before startup, and the Build Failure Analysis workflows were still generated with an older gh-aw compiler.

This change:

- regenerates Issue Triage and both Build Failure Analysis workflows with gh-aw v0.89.15 and Copilot CLI 1.0.83
- pins the generated gh-aw setup action to a full commit SHA

- strict gh-aw compilation and validation passed for all three workflows
- generated action references are pinned to 40-character SHAs

- optional actionlint was not run because Docker was unavailable

Issues.Title: Retry connection resets in Build Failure Analysis setup
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #56224.

Adopt the released gh-aw **v0.87.1 compiler and matching setup runtime** for both Build Failure Analysis entry points. This brings in the existing upstream installer repairs from github/gh-aw#53112 and github/gh-aw#53154 rather than copying or patching an installer in SDK.

- The compatibility-matrix request now retries connection-reset/TLS errors with `--retry-all-errors`.
- Copilot checksum and binary downloads use five retries, a two-second delay, a 60-second retry budget, and `--retry-all-errors`. Downloads still go to files and are SHA256-verified before installation.
- The same runtime also contains the corresponding AWF download retry fix.
- Both the automatic and slash-command workflow locks are regenerated, not hand-edited. The shared source records the exact compiler version and immutable setup SHA needed for reproduction.
- Existing action-cache entries, credential bindings, protected environment, fetch/selection jobs, trigger/concurrency settings, job dependencies/conditions, and permissions are preserved. No authentication fallback or detection bypass is introduced.

## Failure addressed

In [SDK run 34404402939](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/34404402939), the main agent completed successfully. The detection job failed installing Copilot because the compatibility request and then `v1.0.79/SHA256SUMS.txt` failed with `curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`. Ordinary `--retry` did not retry that error class. The subsequent missing executable / missing detection result errors were consequences, not authentication failures.

The full diagnosis is recorded in https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56224#issuecomment-5817140915.

## Why compiler and runtime move together

A runtime-only pin update is not sufficient: the newer setup bundle no longer includes `install_ripgrep.sh`, which the v0.86.2-generated workflows still invoke. Using the matching compiler removes those obsolete calls and emits the runtime's expected setup.

The generated update therefore includes framework changes beyond the curl flags: the Copilot fallback version moves from **1.0.79 to 1.0.80**, AWF from **v0.27.44 to v0.28.1**, and framework safe-output/artifact preparation and error reporting are updated. The BFA prompt body, binlog MCP image/mount, PAT selection/bindings, and inference/write permission boundaries are unchanged.

The v0.87.1 setup action is pinned to `423b3dc04bbf1b1797194a4a75aa5cf5d0d4f5b3`. The existing v0.88.7 cache entry used elsewhere in the repository is retained.

## Validation and limits

- Both workflows compile with v0.87.1 strict mode and schema/action validation. Repeating generation leaves both locks and the shared action cache byte-identical.
- Eight local failure-injection cases use real curl against a loopback TLS endpoint, with the download flags extracted from the old and new immutable installer revisions. The old commands fail immediately on connection resets; the new commands recover. A retried partial download produces the exact expected bytes rather than appended content. Persistent resets and HTTP 404s remain failures after six total attempts.
- Every setup helper referenced by the generated workflows exists in the matching runtime. All 12 setup steps use the intended SHA. Structural comparisons confirm unchanged fetch/selection jobs, authentication expressions, job gates, and permissions.
- Native actionlint v1.7.12 introduces **no new diagnostics**. It still reports the two existing `github.aw.import-inputs.random_seed` expression diagnostics, also reproduced against unchanged upstream `main`. The compiler's Docker-based actionlint could not run because Docker Desktop's Linux daemon was unavailable; the equivalent checksum-verified native release was used, without shellcheck/pyflakes.
- No SDK product code changed; no .NET product build/test suite was run.
- **The changed workflow has not yet been executed end-to-end in `dotnet/sdk`.** The failure-injection results establish the retry behavior, not production inference/report delivery. Permanent download outages still fail explicitly.

Issues.Title: Port runtime PR dotnet/runtime#133111 R2R changes to SDK Crossgen tasks
Issues.Body:
## Why

`dotnet/runtime`'s `src/tasks/Crossgen2Tasks` is a simplified fork of the SDK's shared Crossgen2/ReadyToRun task implementation. A recent runtime PR, dotnet/runtime#133111 ("Use SDK pipeline for WebAssembly framework R2R"), made changes to the shared task logic that were never migrated back into this SDK repo. This PR ports the task-and-target portions of that change that are applicable to the SDK (excluding runtime-only WebCIL/runtime-pack concerns that don't apply here).

## What changed

- **`Microsoft.NET.CrossGen.targets`**: `_CreateR2RImages` now tracks `@(CrossgenTool)`, `@(Crossgen2Tool)`, and the new `@(_ReadyToRunCompilerInputs)` item as incremental inputs, so R2R images are correctly recompiled when the compiler tool or its dependencies change. Both R2R compiler invocations now also forward the runtime-private `$(_PublishReadyToRunCrossgen2ExtraArgs)` property in addition to the existing public `$(PublishReadyToRunCrossgen2ExtraArgs)`.
- **`PrepareForReadyToRunCompilation.cs`**: the R2R output-path helper (previously Mach-O only) now also supports WebAssembly output, since Crossgen2 emits `.wasm` directly for that target. The existing Mach-O behavior (intermediate `.o` compiler output linked into a final `.dylib`) is preserved unchanged for assemblies compiled separately.

## Notable design decision

Only assemblies that are **compiled separately** go through the container-aware output-path helper. Composite component assemblies keep their original publish identity (no extension rewriting, no native-link metadata), matching existing SDK behavior for composite builds. An earlier draft of this change applied the helper uniformly and inadvertently dropped Mach-O native-link metadata for separately-compiled assemblies; this was caught in review and fixed before this PR.

## Testing

Added `test/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests/GivenAPrepareForReadyToRunCompilation.cs` covering:
- WASM output/publish path generation for separately compiled images
- Preserved Mach-O native-link metadata (`.o` -> `.dylib`) for separately compiled images
- Unaffected composite component publish paths/metadata
- The new target-level incremental inputs and private extra-args wiring in `Microsoft.NET.CrossGen.targets`

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx-rc2] Fix dotnet test validation with explicit paths
Issues.Body:
# [release/11.0.1xx-rc2] Fix dotnet test validation with explicit paths

Align no-separator MTP argument handling across .NET 10, RC2, and main.

## Description

The exact #56338 scenario, where test application arguments follow `--`, is already fixed in .NET 11 RC2 by the separator-aware parsing backported in #56207. This PR does not change that behavior.

This PR instead backports the later explicit-build-path validation relaxation from #56375. Without `--`, Microsoft.Testing.Platform extension arguments are still forwarded as unmatched tokens. When an extension option value names an existing `.csproj`, `.sln`, or test module, RC2 can incorrectly treat that value as a non-first positional build path and emit a diagnostic asking the customer to use `--project`, `--solution`, or `--test-modules` even though one of those options is already present.

The change suppresses that misleading diagnostic only when an explicit build-path option has already selected the build input. Positional inference and duplicate build-path validation remain unchanged.

.NET 10 already contains the same no-separator behavior through #56374, so this change aligns .NET 11 RC2 with the merged .NET 10 servicing fix and main.

Coverage includes the end-to-end `--project` scenario with and without `--`, plus direct parser coverage for `--project`, `--solution`, and `--test-modules` in both forms.

RC2 still hosts this logic in `MSBuildUtility.cs`, so the merged `TestCommandOptions.cs` implementation was adapted there without changing behavior.

Related to #56338

## Customer Impact

Customers using Microsoft.Testing.Platform extensions can pass existing project-, solution-, or module-like paths as extension option values consistently with or without `--` when the build input is selected explicitly. The already-supported separator form is unchanged; this backport prevents valid no-separator invocations from failing with a misleading positional-path diagnostic.

## Regression?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Risk

- [ ] High
- [ ] Medium
- [x] Low

The change is narrowly scoped to suppressing a diagnostic only when an explicit build path is already present. Existing positional inference and duplicate build-path validation remain unchanged, and the implementation matches the merged main fix and the behavior already present in .NET 10 servicing.

## Verification

- [ ] Manual
- [x] Automated

- `build.cmd -c Debug` completed with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- A focused `dotnet.Tests` run passed all 8 RC2 cases: two end-to-end `--project` variants and six direct parser variants for all three explicit build-path options with and without `--`.
- The `release/10.0.4xx` branch contains the `!hasExplicitBuildPathOption` validation guard and regression coverage with `[InlineData(false)]` and `[InlineData(true)]`; all #56374 PR checks passed.

Issues.Title: Visual Studio: solution template with .slnx primary output not detected on volumes without 8.3 short names (ReFS Dev Drive), projects added flat instead
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

In Visual Studio, a solution template (`"type": "solution"`, `"editorTreatAs": "solution"`) whose authored solution is a `.slnx` file is only recognised as the created solution on volumes that have **8.3 short file names**. On a ReFS **Dev Drive**, or an NTFS volume with 8.3 names disabled, Visual Studio does not detect the authored `.slnx`. It creates its own solution and adds every generated project to it **flat**, so the authored solution-folder hierarchy is lost. The authored `.slnx` stays on disk, unused, next to it.

On C: (NTFS with 8.3 names), the same template works: VS opens the authored `.slnx`, saves it as `<SolutionName>.slnx` and deletes the original. `dotnet new` (CLI host) is not affected.

The template follows the guidance in [sayedihashimi/template-sample](https://github.com/sayedihashimi/template-sample#solution-templates): the solution is named `<sourceName>.App.slnx`, listed as the only primary output, and renamed for `dotnetcli` hosts only.

I'm filing this here because dotnet/templating now points to this repo. The affected code is in the Visual Studio template host (`Microsoft.VisualStudio.TemplateEngine.VS.dll`), so it may need routing to the VS team.

### Analysis

From the behaviour, and from inspecting `TemplateEngineSolutionHandler.TryGetCreatedSolutionPath` in `Microsoft.VisualStudio.TemplateEngine.VS.dll` 18.10.24.25787, the created solution is found in two steps. Neither step supports `.slnx`:

1. **Primary outputs** are filtered with `Path.EndsWith("sln", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)`. A `.slnx` primary output does not end in `sln`, so it is never considered.
2. **Fallback:** the output folder is enumerated with the search pattern `"*.sln"`. VS runs on .NET Framework, where Win32 wildcard matching also checks 8.3 short names, so `Foo.App.slnx` (short name `FOO~1.SLN`) matches **only when 8.3 names exist**. ReFS has no 8.3 names, and they are disabled by default on non-system NTFS volumes, so on those volumes nothing is found.

With no solution found, the handler falls back to adding every created project to the IDE's solution, which produces the flat result.

`CopyTemplateSolutionFileToUniqueFile` also hard-codes `.sln`.

**Suggested fix:** accept `.slnx` in both steps, e.g. `EndsWith(".sln") || EndsWith(".slnx")`, and enumerate both `*.sln` and `*.slnx`. Also preserve the extension in `CopyTemplateSolutionFileToUniqueFile`.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a solution template with:
   - `"sourceName": "MyTemplate"`, `"tags": { "type": "solution", "editorTreatAs": "solution" }`
   - content: `MyTemplate.App.slnx` containing one or more `<Folder>` elements with projects
   - `"primaryOutputs": [ { "path": "MyTemplate.App.slnx" } ]`
2. `dotnet new install` the template.
3. In Visual Studio, **Create a new project** using the template, with "Place solution and project in the same directory" checked. Choose a location on a **ReFS Dev Drive**, or any volume where `dir /x` shows no short names.
4. Result: two solution files, `<Name>.slnx` (flat, created and opened by VS) and `<Name>.App.slnx` (the authored hierarchy, not opened).
5. Repeat on C: (NTFS with 8.3 names): a single hierarchical `<Name>.slnx` is opened, as expected.

Root-cause check, in Windows PowerShell 5.1 (which runs on .NET Framework, like VS):

```powershell
[IO.Directory]::GetFiles('C:\repos\Acme', '*.sln')   # -> Acme.slnx (matched via short name ACME~1.SLN)
[IO.Directory]::GetFiles('A:\git\Acme', '*.sln')     # -> nothing (ReFS Dev Drive, no short names)
```

In PowerShell 7 (.NET 10), both calls return nothing, because modern .NET matches long names only.

**Expected:** `.slnx` primary outputs are recognised as the created solution on every file system.

### Workaround for template authors

A primary output ending in `sln` passes step 1. VS resolves the primary output by matching it as a glob against the template's source file names, and uses the corresponding target path. So:

- store the authored solution in the template source as `MyTemplate.App.sln`, with `.slnx` XML content
- rename it with source modifiers: to `MyTemplate.App.slnx` for non-CLI hosts, and to `MyTemplate.slnx` for `dotnetcli`
- set `"primaryOutputs": [ { "path": "*.App.sln" } ]`. It must be a wildcard, because a literal path gets `sourceName` substituted and no longer matches the raw source name in the file changes.
- key `specialCustomOperations` on `**/*.sln`

VS then opens the `.slnx` regardless of short names. This relies on undocumented host behaviour, so native `.slnx` support would be much better.

### Further technical details

- Visual Studio Professional 2026 18.10.1 (TemplateEngine host 18.10.24.25787, template engine 8.0.403)
- Windows 11 23H2 (10.0.22631), Dev Drive formatted ReFS
- .NET SDK 11.0.100-preview.6.26359.118 (CLI host unaffected)
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Visual Studio: solution template with .slnx primary output not detected on volumes without 8.3 short names (ReFS Dev Drive), projects added flat instead" (#56391)

Issues.Title: Add Microsoft-internal classification to CLI telemetry
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Port Aspire's Microsoft-internal user/machine classification into the .NET CLI telemetry pipeline.

- add an isolated, BCL-only `Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.InternalMicrosoft` library that owns detection, provider selection, deadlines, result selection, and the six-hour cache
- split each detection mechanism into a focused provider for Windows/WSL domain evidence, Visual Studio accounts, workplace join, macOS Platform SSO, GitHub CLI, Copilot CLI, and environment GitHub credentials
- start classification asynchronously and enrich normal `dotnet-cli` activities from one cached tag set
- support both the managed CLI and Native AOT CLI without coupling the detector library to OpenTelemetry
- document the architecture, privacy rules, cache behavior, and telemetry tags

## Telemetry and privacy behavior

The adapter adds `dotnet.cli.is_microsoft_internal` after detection completes. Positive results can also include the detecting source and locally derived alias/domain. GitHub credentials are used only to query GitHub organization membership and are never cached or emitted. GitHub identity probes are disabled in CI, and alias/domain tags are suppressed in CI.

Detection is bounded, cancellation-aware, failure-safe, and cached for six hours. Failed and timed-out results are not cached. Detector diagnostics remain internal implementation data; this change does not create or export a separate detector activity source.

## Architecture

The classification implementation and telemetry mechanism are intentionally separate:

- `Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.InternalMicrosoft` computes the classification and has no OpenTelemetry dependency.
- `InternalMicrosoftTelemetry` converts the completed result into an immutable tag array that is reused for each activity.
- `InternalMicrosoftTelemetryProcessor` applies those tags to ordinary CLI activities before export.

## Aspire prior art

This is based on Aspire CLI's staged internal-user detection and asynchronous tag enrichment:

- [`InternalMicrosoftDetector`](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/blob/bcdcd4b05edb39210c634101d030404ec18a0a7b/src/Aspire.Cli/Telemetry/InternalMicrosoftDetector.cs)
- [`CliTagEnrichmentProcessor`](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/blob/bcdcd4b05edb39210c634101d030404ec18a0a7b/src/Aspire.Cli/Telemetry/CliTagEnrichmentProcessor.cs)

The SDK port keeps the same core signals while factoring detection into its own AOT-compatible library and per-signal providers.

## Validation

- `build.cmd`
- `.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build src\Cli\dotnet\dotnet.csproj -c Debug`
- `.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build src\Cli\dotnet-aot\dotnet-aot.csproj -c Debug`
- `.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~InternalMicrosoftDetectorTests"` (23 passed)
- `git diff --check`
